https://www.thetimes.com/uk/transport/ar.title: HS2 Euston tunnel protesters hail from ‘off-grid’ Scottish island Gometra
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/transport/ar.text:
Two of the HS2 protesters holed up in tunnels dug in secret near Euston station are children of the millionaire owner of a remote British island.
Blue and Lazer Sandford, 18 and 20, are committed Extinction Rebellion campaigners who live part-time on Gometra, in the Inner Hebrides. The island has no cars, mains electricity or internet in homes.
Roc Sandford, their father, is a landowner and publisher who often joins them at protests. A climate activist himself, he recently gave his children Christmas presents made out of rubbish he found on Gometra that he reclaimed into art and wrapped in old newspaper.
The siblings, real names Isla and Lachlan, are among a group of campaigners called HS2 Rebellion who have spent months digging a network of tunnels in Euston Square Gardens in London to delay the development of the high-speed railway line.
Following news reports about the tunnels on Tuesday night, bailiffs arrived to evict them early on Wednesday, prompting a small number of protesters to retreat and barricade themselves 15ft below ground.
Lazer released a video from inside the tunnel system yesterday morning saying that the protesters had experienced “torturous conditions” overnight as the bailiffs deprived them of sleep. “They have kept us constantly awake with loud noises, they’ve been shining bright lights down in our faces, rocks have fallen on my head,” he said.
Blue had posted a photograph of herself and Lazer huddled together in an underground chamber on Instagram hours earlier, with the caption: “I put the crime in criminal.”
She has been dubbed the British Greta Thunberg because of her activism with the youth wing of Extinction Rebellion but rejects the comparison with the Swedish climate activist, who is also 18, because “it’s making it about individuals rather than the movement”.
On Gometra, where the pair sometimes live with their father, 21-year-old sister and a fourth sibling, when they are not with their mother in west London, electricity is generated from wind and hydro power.
In a blog written when she was 16, Blue said her family have “always tried to live in a particularly environmentally conscious way — we try not to use central heating, or buy clothes first hand and most of us are at varying stages of vegetarian/veganism”.
She was introduced to climate activism aged nine, when her father campaigned against “an environmentally degrading salmon farm” proposed off the northwest coast of Gometra.
She said they “received threats that their houses would be burnt down, were physically threatened with violence and ostracised from the community”. She added: “For the first time I encountered the ‘opposition’ to environmentalism.”
Since Blue became a prominent climate campaigner, her father has registered a new company called Blue Rebellion with Companies House. Its two directors are Extinction Rebellion leaders. Mr Sandford did not respond to a request for comment.
Grant Shapps, the transport secretary, described the tunnellers’ actions as “reckless, irresponsible and deeply concerning”.
The National Eviction Team, which is carrying out the operation for HS2, had evicted most of the protesters who occupied treetops at the site by yesterday afternoon.
It said that the “inexperienced” activists risked a tunnel collapse and intercepting gas and water pipes, “leading to risks of suffocation, flooding and drowning”.
